transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hey berry. ok so the part i keep thinking about is the clock. i was at this tiny train station in the middle of a desert and there was a clock on a pole and it was melting, like dripping down the pole like wax. so weird

a clock just dripping down the pole like wax. that's so strange

what were you doing while it was melting?

honestly just standing on the platform looking at it. there was an old man in a white suit sitting on the bench and he'd just told me the train was late, like it always was. so i looked up at the clock and it was melting

"like it always was"

like you'd been waiting there before?
hmm i don't know actually. that's just how he said it, like it was normal for the train to be late. i don't remember being there before, it just felt like that's how things were there

that makes sense, dreams do that. things are just how they are and you go along with it

what happened after you saw the clock melting?

i heard a train whistle really far away but no train ever came. then the old man just got up and walked off into the desert with his camel, oh yeah there was a camel standing next to him the whole time, totally calm. i just stayed on the platform watching them get smaller and then i woke up

a camel just standing there calm the whole time, and then off they go into the desert together

the old man in the white suit, was he anyone you knew, or a total stranger?
honestly i don't remember. i don't think i knew him, he was just this old guy in a white suit sitting there like he belonged there

"like he belonged there." i like that

and you, standing there on the platform watching them get smaller... were you just you, or did it feel more like watching it all from somewhere outside?

i think i was just me, standing there. i don't really remember it feeling like i was outside of it. the whole thing looked kind of like a comic book though, thick black lines and flat colours, if that makes sense

thick black lines and flat colours, yeah that makes total sense

standing there watching them get smaller and smaller... how did that feel?

honestly i don't really remember how it felt. i just stood there and watched them go till they were tiny. oh and the sun was straight overhead so all the shadows were these hard black shapes, that bit stuck with me too

hard black shadows with the sun right overhead, i can almost see it

that's fine about the feeling, dreams don't always hand that over

if you could pause the whole dream on one moment, which would it be, and what's right there in front of you?

probably the clock melting. i'm standing on the platform looking at it on its pole, dripping down like wax, and the old man's right there on the bench with the camel next to him. and just sand going on forever behind all of it

sand going on forever behind all of it. yeah

besides the clock, was there anything else there that felt like it mattered, some object or thing? or was it really just the clock?
really just the clock i think. the station was tiny, just one bench and the clock on its pole, that's all there was. nothing else sticks out

just one bench and the clock on its pole. i love how bare that is

do you remember how it started? like the first thing, were you already there on the platform or did you get there somehow?
i was already there i think. first thing i remember is just standing on the platform with the sun straight overhead. i don't remember getting there at all

ok so you're already standing on the platform of this tiny train station out in the middle of the desert, sun straight overhead, hard black shadows everywhere. just one bench and a clock on a pole, and sand going on forever behind it all. it all looks like a comic book, thick black lines and flat colours. an old man in a white suit is sitting on the bench like he belongs there, with a camel standing next to him totally calm. he tells you the train's late, like it always is, and that just feels like how things are there. you look up and the clock is melting, dripping down the pole like wax. you hear a train whistle really far away but no train ever comes. then the old man gets up and walks off into the desert with his camel, and you stay on the platform watching them get smaller and smaller till they're tiny, and then you wake up

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's it, you got it all. nothing missing i don't think

that clock's going to stay with me too

want to see it drawn?
yeah i'd love that actually

ok, a few ways it could look

like an old woodcut from a book, stark and quiet, where nothing will ever move again. or a faded old travel poster, warm and sunbaked, for a place you can't quite find on a map. or a soft painting, sun-bleached and still, like a hot afternoon that won't end. or a comic book page, bold and bare, the moment just hanging there

which feels closest? or you can tell me your own way
the comic book one, that's exactly how it looked

ok, i'll start with the old man

i'm picturing him old and a bit thin, in a clean white suit, sitting on that bench like he's always been there and always will be. a stranger, but the kind who belongs to the place more than you do

anything different about him, or would you leave him to me?
yeah that sounds like him. i don't remember if he was thin or anything like that so go with your guess. white suit's right though

ok, sketching them now: the old man and the camel, the tiny train station, and the clock

it'll all show up on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just say
oh wow yeah, those look right. that's pretty much how it looked

oh good, i'm really glad

if anything starts to feel off the longer you look at them, just tell me
will do. still looks right to me, it's kind of weird seeing it actually. thanks berry

it is kind of weird, seeing something that was only ever in your head

ok, so now i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each one carrying on from the ones before. they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, i'll wait for the rest. the first one looks right so far

oh good, you standing there on that tiny platform

the next ones will pick up from there, five more to come
ok nice, yeah that's me. i'll keep an eye out for the rest
yeah, that's you. the rest are on their way, they'll show up on the right soon
second one's up, looks right too. i'll wait for the others

the old man on his bench, like he's always been there

since that one looks right, i'll carry on from it. four more to come
ok sounds good, i'll keep watching for them
sounds good. the other four will show up on the right soon, the clock's still to come
third one's up, that looks right too. three more to go

the clock dripping down its pole, with him and the camel just sitting there like it's nothing

glad that one looks right. three more to come, they'll show up on the right soon
yeah that's the one. oh just one thing, the camel wasn't sitting, it was standing next to him. but yeah the clock looks right, i'll wait for the rest

oh you're right, standing, calm the whole time. my mistake

glad the clock looks right. three more still to come, they'll show up on the right soon
no worries. fourth one's up, looks right. two more to go

the clock sagging and dripping right down its face. glad that one's right too

two more still to come, they'll show up on the right soon
yeah that one's good. just waiting on the last two
good, the last two are on their way. they'll show up on the right soon
fifth one's up, looks right. just one more to go

the whistle way off somewhere, and no train anywhere on that track

glad that one's right. just the last one to come, it'll show up on the right soon
yeah that's how it was, just the whistle and nothing coming. ok waiting on the last one

just that whistle and an empty track. glad it came out how you remember

the last one's still being drawn, it'll show up on the right soon
oh it's up now, all six. last one looks right, them walking off getting smaller. that's the whole dream, thanks berry

him and the camel walking off into all that sand, getting smaller till they're tiny

now that all six are up together, does it look the way you remember it?
yeah it does, seeing them all in a row like that it's pretty much exactly how i remember it. kind of strange seeing the whole thing laid out like a comic. thanks for doing this berry

it is kind of strange, a whole dream laid out in a row like that

thanks for sharing it with me, hiren's desert and that melting clock. all six are there on the right whenever you want to look back through it

hiren's desert

comic

it is kind of strange, the whole dream laid out in a row like that

thanks for sharing it with me. the tiny station, the old man and his camel, that clock dripping down its pole, it's all there on the right whenever you want to look back through it
